dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Gemstones reflect the light differently in different environments.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: A gem by candlelight flickers like flame, while a jewel beneath the moon seems like a tear-filled eye.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: There are a thousand forms to beauty, and gems are cut a thousand ways. Such is the complexity of things both elegant and timeless.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I'm in the habit of collecting these old gemstones. Some are even from other nations. Feel free to enjoy this collection whenever you please.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Being as old as they are, they have lost some of their glow and appear a little turbid. They cannot compare with the brilliant luster of a newly-cut stone.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Do be careful when touching them. So as to not damage them, I've left most of them in their original casing.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Another three reports finished. Time for a breath of fresh air.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Do they make you write reports in the Adventurers' Guild, too?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: How very fortunate... Remember to count your blessings.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I have never been able to get used to the endless cycle of report after report. I daresay we had no such custom in the Nod-Krai of old.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Of course, I understand why they are important, but this process of repeatedly describing in laborious detail things that could easily be summarized in a single sentence... it is exhausting.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: The mere thought of the outstanding reports I have yet to finish is simply—

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: No, I mustn't. These things are necessary — I should focus on that. A dutiful Ratnik must write his reports.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: A little longer here, and then I'll get back to it. Just a little longer...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ugh... Alas. Then we share the same misfortune.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Shh, a little lighter on your feet, if you wouldn't mind.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The fish here are used to the quiet, which makes them very sensitive indeed to external noise.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: So, as well as treading gently, we ought to keep our voices down when we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I once tried fishing while two ghosts nearby were chatting incessantly. Didn't get a single bite all day.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Since then, I have resolved to greet any nearby ghosts and ask them to kindly take their conversation elsewhere before I begin.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I very much wish to see fish on the dinner table tonight. I shall not go home empty-handed.
